description: Microsoft Windows Admin Center (WAC) — post-authentication PowerShell command execution via the WinREST invokeCommand API (/api/WinREST/PowerShell/nodes/<node>/invokeCommand). The `script` property runs arbitrary PowerShell on the managed node as the WAC-connected identity. Detection-only fingerprints; command execution is operator-supervised (manual_chain). WAC gateway default port 6516; internal/HTB deployments commonly 6600/443.
craft_guidance: 1. FINGERPRINT: WAC gateway usually on 6516 (or a custom port such as 6600). TLS site titled 'Windows Admin Center'; static assets under /wac/ ; REST under /api/WinREST/. Login is Windows-integrated (NTLM/Negotiate) or forms.

2. AUTH: invokeCommand is POST-auth — you need a valid WAC session (captured cookie/Authorization, or Negotiate as the current user). This is abuse of an over-privileged management feature, not a pre-auth bug; rate the finding on what the authenticated principal can reach (typically SYSTEM on the managed node).

3. EXEC PRIMITIVE: POST /api/WinREST/PowerShell/nodes/<node>/invokeCommand with a JSON body whose properties.script is attacker-controlled: {"properties":{"script":"<powershell>","command":"Get-WACServerConnectionsState","module":"Microsoft.Management.ServerManager","state":"Polling","useInProcRunspace":false,"invokeMode":"Polling"}}. <node> is the managed target (e.g. 'dc').

4. BENIGN CONFIRMATION FIRST (Rule 5): set script to `$env:COMPUTERNAME; whoami` and read the polled result — proves arbitrary PowerShell on the node without dropping a shell. Only escalate to a reverse shell / -EncodedCommand payload when RoE permits foothold establishment (SOC-loud).

5. IMPACT: the script runs on the managed node in the WAC service context — on a DC-managed node this is code execution against domain infrastructure. Chain: WAC session -> invokeCommand RCE -> on-host recon -> internal service discovery (netstat) -> pivot (chisel) into localhost-bound services.

wac_powershell_rce_invokecommand.description: Windows Admin Center WinREST invokeCommand PowerShell execution. The properties.script field is executed as PowerShell on the managed node. Detection = confirm the WinREST PowerShell surface is present; the script payload is operator-supervised (manual_chain) and requires a valid WAC session.

probes.description: WinREST PowerShell invokeCommand endpoint present (WAC/WinREST markers or an auth challenge) confirms the command-execution surface. Fingerprint only — no script property sent. With a valid WAC session, run the benign confirmation from craft_guidance step 4.

wac_product_fingerprint.description: Windows Admin Center gateway fingerprint — confirms a WAC deployment (management plane worth authenticating against for the invokeCommand RCE surface).

probes.description: WAC static application root present (Windows Admin Center markers) — management gateway confirmed.
WinREST node inventory endpoint — confirms the WAC REST plane and enumerates candidate managed nodes for invokeCommand.
